where: helpers.js: ability-timing with at; RULE_KEYS from columns.json; unit-ref; faction-allies
why: Mostly right. ability-timing with at only changes the 13 keys whose ability has at. RULE_KEYS from columns.json gives the old list minus tag and ask plus at and tableAt; no rule has ask (columns.json has no such column). Leaving mods, aura and guard out is right: all 14 faction-level readings match an approved unit-footnote, aura or guard item exactly. 459 stale = 441 + 13 ability-timing re-keyed by at + 5 rule-tag dropped. I checked this by running a941f16's helpers.js on the same data: the 18 approved keys gone are exactly those, and the 30 new keys are rule-at 9, rule-tableAt 1, ability-timing 13, unit-ref 4, faction-allies 3. Three problems remain: dropping tag, the unit-ref source and the faction-allies source.
fix: verify/helpers.js has three fixes. (1) RULE_KEYS: keep tag, i.e. `.map(([c]) => c)))].concat('tag'))`. Relentless Rage's tag "Already in A" is the app's own judgement (data.js:514, with its note); New Recruit does not print it, so it must stay signed. The four "Once per…" tags are harmless to keep signed. Their 5 old approvals come back with the same keys, and stale drops to 441. (2) unit-ref: cite the unit that has the rule, not the reference sheet, `if(u.ref) add(a.id, 'unit-ref', w, { ref:u.ref }, cited(a.id, a.units.find(x => x.id === u.ref.by) || u, { from:u.ref.rule || u.ref.strat }));`. Today 3 of the 4 items have source {"missing":"nothing in the data is named …"}, so a change to Split, Seed Spore Mines or the Pink Horrors ability would not void their sign-off. (3) faction-allies: look the rule up among the faction's army and detachment rules too. Mission Tactics is the Deathwatch Support detachment rule, so today its source is "Mission Tactics: " (empty). Use `{ rules:Object.values(f.allies).map(n => n + ': ' + (D.rules[n] || f.armyRules.concat(Object.values(f.detachments).flatMap(detRules_)).filter(r => r.name === n).map(r => r.text).join('\n'))) }`.

where: unit-ref · tzeeeeentch · Blue Horrors
why: The judgement is right: the quote is in fluxmaster-pink-horrors's "Horrors are Pink. Horrors are Blue. Where once there was one, now there are two." word for word (checked against data.js). But the item's source is {"missing":"nothing in the data is named Horrors are Pink. Horrors are Blue. Where once there was one, now there are two."}, because cited() looks in the reference sheet's own abilities, not those of the ref.by unit. So the key does not hold the rule text, and a change to that text would not void the sign-off. Apply the unit-ref fix in helpers.js (code item 484c49a360a79ac2); this same judgement then gets a new key, which approve.js approves as this fix.

ref.rule: Horrors are Pink. Horrors are Blue. Where once there was one, now there are two.
ref.quote: If, at any point, this unit contains no PINK HORROR models, use the BLUE HORRORS datasheet for this unit.
